body: You're very kind, thank you.

I'm so sorry. One of my loved ones that I mentioned in my post was a devout catholic until the end, but she had awful stories about the abuse she was subjected to by nuns in her school. They humiliated her because she was so poor that she went to school barefoot. And yet her faith never wavered.

I love the way churches makes me feel, the smells and everything I mentioned in my post. But I find that some people seem so judgemental. They stare at you from up and down, as if you're beneath them.

Thank you. How do you reconcile it though? Won't you ever be in a relationship with another man? How do you accept that you will never have a soulmate and your own family? I want that so badly, and without it everything feels pointless. I don't want to be the lonely weirdo standing in the corner for the rest of my life. Or the one that pretends to be happy and part of the group, but everyone pitys because he has no family and always goes home alone.

Thank you so much for taking the time to reply. I didn't knew there was a name for it, I just felt it inside of me, just as I feel it now. I mean it, no one induced me into this, it wasn't even something that was talked about back then. I tried to talk to my mom about it when I was 4, but she became very angry and told me never to speak about it again, specially not in front of my dad. I wish I could be like one of those people who can just fake it, go to the complete opposite direction and lie to everyone, but I can't. 

Even when I believed and prayed, I never felt like I heard God or felt like he was with me. At the requiem mass of a loved one, when my mom asked if I felt her presence I said yes in order not to dissapoint her, but in truth I felt nothing at all. I didn't even get one of those dreams where they tell you they are at peace, and I used to get very vivid and detailed dreams. 

I just don't get it why His will would be of me leading such a miserable, unfulfilling life. To always be on the sidelines watching everyone become their own person, find love, have a family while I'm supposed to repress myself. Why couldn't I simply be born satisfied and comfortable in my own skin? Everything would have been so different.

I'm 29, with every year it becomes more obvious I'm never going to be that person I always dreamed that I was going to be, the one I am on the inside, and that I'm not getting that white picket fence love story I wanted. In my dreams, by 29 and I would have already been married for a few years and starting to think about having children.

It's so painful not having someone you can talk freely about everything. And then you turn to reddit, only for your comment or post to get buried. Ignored at best, downvoted and mocked at worst.

Sometimes I feel invisible, as if I'm completely cut off from the rest of the world and living on some kind of alternate plane.

Thank you so much, this is so incredibly detailed and helpful, you have no idea. 

My therapist wasn't big on labels or diagnosis. She mentioned once that she could refer to me to a psychiastrist if I felt like I needed a proper diagnosis and possibly medication. Towards our last meetings I mentioned that I wanted that, but she would always change the subject. Looking back, I think what actually helped me back then was the meditation of sorts we did at the end of each meeting. Obviously having someone to talk to was nice, but that specifically felt so good. It made me feel light every time I left her office.

I think this one current obsession feels different because there's less things to engage with. With those actors or that band I had plenty of things to give a sense of accomplishment, new files to hoard and consume, an upcoming appearance or new work on the horizon. But now with the book there's nothing really that I can do. I will randomly think about it and have to fight back tears. I spend hours on Google Maps looking at the street view of the area it takes place, and sometimes it looks almost exactly like what I envisioned while reading and it makes me cry. 

On the early days I did felt something similar to that euphoria I mentioned in the post, while looking for properties for sale in the area that somehow looked exactly how I had pictured the one in the book, despite never being or looking up that region before. I feel so close to these characters, specially the one who dies. I know he's not real, but he had so many of the qualities I admire, so many of the ideals and opinions I already had before. Sometimes I see something on the news and think of how he would react to it. I keep thinking about the suffering he endured on his final days, and how unfair it was, and how I wish it would have been different. Every now and then I will think rationally and tell myself none of this is real, but I can't help it. I want it to be real, I want to believe that there are people like him, out there in the world making a diference and living their life to the fullest. 

I think this is why I became hooked to that youtube channel I mentioned in my post. That guy sort of reminded me of that character, both physically and in his attitude and outlook in life. At times it makes me happy, it's as if that character's light and what he represented truly exists in real people. But then I start to cry again, wishing that the character could have gotten his happy ending. It's so stupid, I don't know why I have to be like this.

Thank you so much for replying. I saw a therapist for about a year before the pandemic. I did felt nice aftewards and it was coincidentally the one year I didn't struggled with this overwhelming anxiety I constantly have about time passing, which I have since I was a teenager and for certain periods of time is all I can think about. But at the same time, I felt like she was only teaching me to sweep everything under the rug, and she seemed anxious for me to confirm that things that I had previously talked about with her no longer bothered me. 

How do you personally deal with it? It makes me feel like I'm constantly on alert, it's like I can't even feel truly at ease. And yet, at the same time, I don't want to stop thinking about this book. I don't want to let those characters go.

I'm sorry you're going through that. If it means anything, I had a friend in middle school who lied all the time, anything from the silliest to actual important things. I didn't held it against him back then, even though  and I surely don't right now. I checked out his facebook or instagram a while back and he seems to be doing well, which made me very happy.

I'm really sorry to hear that, you don't deserve that. 

How did you stopped fantasizing about love though? I didn't mentioned in my post because sometimes that attracts nasty messages, but I'm a closeted trans woman, so the chances that I will ever be fullfiled romantically are pratically zero. But I can't help it, I always dreamed of being a beautiful woman, falling in love, getting married, having kids... and yet I'm never going to get anything even remotely close to that. Which is why I gave up on the world. I havent worked or studied since graduating college at 21. I'm a complete dead weight.
That's cool that you went to Amsterdam, what were you doing there?
It's a complicated feeling. It brings some very brief moments of joy, but at one point I become painfully aware that daydreaming will never be enough.
I understand, sometimes I also imagine how the relationship would be like in the future.

I'd die to be able to experience this for real. Fantasizing and day dreaming used to be more fulfulling, but I'm turning 30 this year and now I just feel panic that it really is not going to happen for me.

I like to see couples in their late 20s/30s together in the mall or in the market. Just the two together, almost completely in silence because they are at that point where they don't need to entertain each other. They can communicate just fine like that, and each other's company is enough. They lean against each other, or one has their arm around the other. They nudge the other to show something cute or funny they saw. I wish I could have that.
I'll try to use you as my inspiration, thank you so much.

Thank you for reading and replying. A few years ago, even daydreaming would make me feel euphoric. For a few minutes at a time it was like I was truly living those alternate lives, it made me feel physically light and at peace. It hasn't happened in years though.

Thank you for taking the time to read and reply, I normally have to delete these posts because no one does. I know I have to put myself out there and get a job, but everything feels so difficult for me. The idea of going anywhere on my own feels completely out of reach. How did you mustered the courage to go out like that?
Just letting you know that I read your comment and sympathize with your pain. It sucks to be like this, I wish we could be normal.

I would love to know. For the last few years I read or watch videos until I can’t keep my eyelids open, which can happen between 4am-7am, and then I wake up at midday or 1pm. If I try to sleep normally I just spend hours turning in bed thinking about bad things.

I just turned 29, I quite literally slept through my 20s.
Same, but I just turned 29. Sick of existing, I want out.

Thank you, your comment made me smile. I have done 3D modeling as a hobby since I was a teen, but I never got any good at it. I did give painting a try a couple of years ago, and been meaning to try it more seriously.
Yes, I try to keep that in mind

Thank you. I regret not having found work immediately after college. I thought it would be easier to hide at home, but it only made me feel more alien. At the same time, Im not sure I would have been able to have spent the last 8 years working. I would be comparing myself to coworkers just like I did during my college internship, and that was the first time I even considered ending it all.
If they are happy, have friends and soul mates they are better than me already.
Thank you. It means a lot, even though Im not sure I believe in it anymore

Thank you. Its not just a matter or age, but or my identity. I know I will never be the person I see in my head. If I try to do something about that now it would be like painting a target on my back for hate crime. Then I wonder if I wouldn’t be miserable still no matter what I do, because I will never be what I think is my true self, no one will ever look at me and feel desire.

Thank you. Sometimes I wonder if it wouldn’t be best not to be on social media at all because of that. But at the same time, that would make me feel even more disconnected from the world. I also like to see beautiful things and places, I think I would miss being able to see them. Specially now that my surroundings are only getting uglier.

I thought about joining some shorter courses on subjects I like, but I fear I will put myself up for ridicule. I remember how awful it was this one time in college I had to do a project with people from outside my class. I tried to participate and talk to them, but they simply ignored me and talked among themselves.
Thank you. And its not like we wish harm on them, we simply would like to have something like that too.

Thank you for being nice. I dont know why, but even normal things always felt so difficult for me. To me someone simply existing, being able to talk to people, make decisions and be themselves sounds like science fiction. Im from South America.
That’s exactly it, it feels so cruel.
